concepts.title: Similarity in Change (Proportional Change)
concepts.definition: Two pictures or quantities look similar after resizing only when every measurement changes by the same multiplication factor; shrinking both width and height by half keeps a photograph's shape, while removing the same amount from each distorts it because the factors differ.
concepts.formula: similar change: width_new = width_old * factor and height_new = height_old * factor
concepts.key_idea: Same factor on every measure keeps the shape; equal subtraction does not.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp107.txt lines 1-70 (images A to E, factor comparison)
question_patterns: why do images A, C and D look similar while B and E look distorted

solution_steps.action: find the change factor of the width
solution_steps.explain: Divide the new width by the old width.

solution_steps.action: find the change factor of the height
solution_steps.explain: Divide the new height by the old height.
Equal factors mean a proportional change and a similar shape; unequal factors mean distortion.

concepts.title: Ratios and Proportion
concepts.definition: A ratio a : b compares two quantities term by term, saying there are b units of the second for every a units of the first; two ratios are proportional when one is a uniform multiple of the other, written a : b :: c : d.
concepts.key_idea: 60 : 40 :: 30 : 20 :: 90 : 60 - the width to height ratio is the same for similar images.

solution_steps.explain: Put each comparison in the form first term : second term.

A single common factor lets you write the two ratios with the proportion symbol.

concepts.title: Simplest Form of a Ratio
concepts.definition: Dividing both terms of a ratio by their highest common factor gives its simplest form, and two ratios are proportional exactly when their simplest forms match; 60 : 40 reduces by 20 to 3 : 2, the same as 90 : 60 reduced by 30.
concepts.formula: red_a = term_a / hcf; red_b = term_b / hcf
concepts.key_idea: Reduce each ratio by its HCF; identical simplest forms mean the ratios are in proportion.

solution_steps.explain: Divide the first term by the HCF of the two terms.
Divide the second term by the same HCF to keep the ratio fair.

concepts.title: Missing Value in a Proportion
concepts.definition: When two ratios are known to be proportional, an unknown term is recovered by keeping the same multiplier: if a : b equals c : x, then x equals c times b divided by a, the unitary reasoning behind bus counts, recipe scaling and price comparisons.
concepts.key_idea: Scale the known pair: 3 : 4 :: 72 : 96 because 72 and 96 both grow by 24.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp107.txt lines 124-160 (Example 1), 613-787 (sharing and problems), Figure it Out bus example

solution_steps.action: apply the known term of the second ratio
solution_steps.explain: The unknown grows from c the way b grows from a.

solution_steps.explain: Dividing by a completes the unitary scaling.

concepts.title: Sharing a Whole in a Given Ratio
concepts.definition: To divide a total in a ratio such as 3 : 1, split the total into equal groups the size of the sum of the ratio terms and hand out groups in that pattern; 12 counters in ratio 3 : 1 become 9 and 3 because the whole is three groups of 4.
concepts.formula: group = total / (part_a + part_b); share_a = group * part_a
concepts.key_idea: 42 in ratio 4 : 3 means 42 split into 7 groups of 6, giving 24 and 18.
question_patterns: share 42 counters between two people in the ratio 4 : 3

solution_steps.action: find the size of one equal group
solution_steps.explain: Divide the total by the sum of the ratio terms.
Each person receives their term count times the group size.

concepts.title: Unit Conversions and Temperature
concepts.definition: Proportional reasoning often needs unit changes: metres to feet, litres to millilitres, and temperature via the linear rules Fahrenheit = 9/5 x Celsius + 32 and Celsius = 5/9 x (Fahrenheit - 32); 25 degrees Celsius converts to 77 degrees Fahrenheit.
concepts.key_idea: Temperature is not a plain ratio - shift by 32 handles the freezing-point offset.
question_patterns: convert 25 degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the Celsius reading by 9 and divide by 5.
